items.Composition interactions: Social character changes tenure, stall form and who benefits; optional traits can disrupt access or create special goods. Trade competes with, rather than automatically replacing, housing and other uses.
items.Core idea: Trade and exchange organize the district's livelihood.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual inhabitants or visiting traders and reachable suppliers, routes or meaningful market demand.
items.Generative effects: Market grounds, public approaches, freight/merchant frontage, storage and variable retail intensity; produces real POI destinations.
items.Name: Market Exchange
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor route junctions, clientele, institutional/chartered exchanges and multi-route trading reach; downweight isolated poorly supplied land.

items.Composition interactions: Social guild/estate/tenement character changes ownership and workshop size; hazards and magical traits affect materials/space, not automatic new craft capability.
items.Core idea: Workshops, repair, manufacture and skilled trades support residents.
items.Eligibility requirements: Suitable labor/skill traditions, accessible inputs, customers or partners and tolerable working ground.
items.Generative effects: Workshop-yard concentrations, service passages, stores, trade schools/guild halls where supported, localized nuisance and apprenticeship POIs.
items.Name: Craft & Workshops
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor service corridors, productive suppliers, guild ties, material resources, market contact and shared equipment.

items.Composition interactions: Noble/communal/crowded residents organize freight differently; ruins/walls alter gates and chokepoints; never add an ungrounded harbor.
items.Core idea: Storage and handling of goods dominate local productive life.
items.Eligibility requirements: A connected regional road, landing, harbor, canal or other genuine freight transfer and goods flow.
items.Generative effects: Large handling yards, warehousing, distinct freight access/road geometry, landings or depots where terrain supports them.
items.Name: Freight Hub
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor navigable water, paired transport modes, heavy route convergence and external trade; inland wagon depots remain possible.

items.Composition interactions: A tenement's street food differs from an estate's provision yards; springs, animal presence and flood risks modify sites and use.
items.Core idea: Markets, growers and food-processing livelihoods feed the city.
items.Eligibility requirements: Reachable food or arable/working land, water where needed, and actual provisioning demand.
items.Generative effects: Milling/baking/brewing/food markets, kitchen yards, supply roads, gardens or produce courts with genuine area and inputs.
items.Name: Food Provisioning
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor agricultural fringe, mills, inns, markets, kitchens, fisheries or importing corridors according to site.

items.Composition interactions: A separate social selection determines crowding, rights and organization; magical or historic traits can create local anomalies without replacing ordinary livelihood.
items.Core idea: Residential services and ordinary local livelihoods predominate, without implying a social class.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual settled population, available housing/built stock and reachable basic supplies/services.
items.Generative effects: Dwellings at City scale as built intensity, local service commons, inns, healers or shops when warranted; never a single repeated generic POI.
items.Name: Household Services
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor lived-in areas that lack an overriding productive specialization; viable baseline for many inland towns.

items.Composition interactions: Social selection controls access/tenure; ancient ruins can attract scholars if evidence and clients exist. Do not spam academy POIs merely because a district is learned.
items.Core idea: Scribes, teachers, healers, skilled knowledge workers and institutional services cluster.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual schools, patrons, learning tradition, archive, medical needs or equivalent documented expertise; magical services require real practitioners/medium.
items.Generative effects: Academies, halls, scriptoria, clinics, libraries or specialized services with meaningful grounds, where actually supported.
items.Name: Scholarly & Professional Services
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor connected patrons, civic or religious institutions, retained archives, specialist skilled residents and visiting clients.

items.Composition interactions: With markets produces crowded bazaars; with learned services can yield cramped boarding/study halls. Hazards or boons operate through existing physical facts.
items.Core idea: Densely occupied households with constrained space, resources or rights.
items.Eligibility requirements: Occupied population, limited housing/land and credible crowding or low-capital conditions.
items.Generative effects: Compact housing areas, small commons, narrow/indirect approaches at Street resolution, reduced private grounds and dense local service demand.
items.Name: Crowded Tenements
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor steep land pressure, livelihood dependence and limited capital; not an automatic synonym for crime or poverty.

items.Composition interactions: Freight/market identities require negotiation with exclusive ground; ruined walls or magical features change defenses and prestige.
items.Core idea: Wealthy or politically privileged households retain spacious holdings and controlled space.
items.Eligibility requirements: Existing substantial wealth, tenure, political privilege or sponsor relationships that can support reserved land.
items.Generative effects: Separated compounds, private gardens, prominent avenues, controlled access and a few significant estate/civic POIs.
items.Name: Patrician Estates
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor high investment, secure rights, valued access/view, courts or elite institutions; exclude when no supportive social/economic evidence.

items.Composition interactions: With crafts forms working quarters; with market becomes guild-governed trading; with ruins/animals adapts shared rights and service costs.
items.Core idea: Craft, trade or service corporations share governance and productive infrastructure.
items.Eligibility requirements: Grounded guild/trade institutions, common workshop services or durable cooperative rights.
items.Generative effects: Collective yards, common halls, meeting courts, shared service approaches and contested jurisdiction edges.
items.Name: Guild Commons
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor dense professional links, shared machinery/service access, guild halls, negotiated working commons.

items.Composition interactions: Combines with either affluent or tenement-like housing pressures via actual resources, not automatic stereotyping; external historic ties matter.
items.Core idea: Migrants, refugees or visiting communities maintain a distinct local social network.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual immigration, displacement, trade-connected visiting communities or documented resident contacts; do not assume migrants are poor or unwanted.
items.Generative effects: Arrival lodgings, community commons, diverse services, linked entrances and culturally meaningful POIs where supported.
items.Name: Newcomer Quarter
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor arrival roads, existing contacts, affordable/supportive residences, communal institutions and historical settlement routes.

items.Composition interactions: Market/crafts/provision identities become civic or cooperative variations; conflict with elite enclosure claims can shape boundaries.
items.Core idea: Independent or communal households coordinate rights and shared civic spaces.
items.Eligibility requirements: Established civilian households or community rights with legal/social support; no invented charter or polity.
items.Generative effects: Shared courts, greens, publicly accessible service connections, collectively protected space and ward institutions where grounded.
items.Name: Free Commons
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor open access, mutual services, citizen assemblies, commons tenure and local stewardship.

items.Composition interactions: Market/tenement/estate effects differ according to risk and access; let movement, hazards and any legitimate stable crossing respond through shared questions.
items.Core idea: A local Veil phenomenon distorts ordinary geography or access.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual Veil medium/discontinuity in inherited physical/magical state; stable travel only with established paired destinations/keepers.
items.Generative effects: Locally altered passability, protected approach, disruption or special waiting/holding space; no automatic portal.
items.Name: Veil Discontinuity
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Increase weight near real Veil features, supported maintainers and meaningful route/terrain interference.

items.Composition interactions: Changes workshop/estate/commons occupation and maintenance; cannot create vegetation without substrate.
items.Core idea: Magically responsive or unusually vigorous vegetation invades urban ground.
items.Eligibility requirements: Real Greenwood influence plus viable rooting/water/ecological substrate and local history.
items.Generative effects: Overgrown courtyards, living canopy corridors, negotiated orchard/common claims or abandoned grounds.
items.Name: Greenwood Encroachment
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor old gardens, water and maintained or abandoned structures with Greenwood signals.

items.Composition interactions: With civic/scholarly economy creates witness or archive uses only with real patrons; local culture and tenure decide access.
items.Core idea: Ancestral, funerary or preserved remains occupy significant settlement space.
items.Eligibility requirements: Real burial/history, Salt-bearing preservation or cultural custodianship where appropriate; no invented necropolis.
items.Generative effects: Processional paths, preserved walls/courts, sacred open ground and constrained development near actual graves.
items.Name: Salt Ossuary
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor extant old burial sites, grave stewardship, memorial routes and preserved material.

items.Composition interactions: Trade and low-capital housing create differing adaptations; no arbitrary disaster replay on the World timeline.
items.Core idea: Recurring inundation affects livelihoods, access and building history.
items.Eligibility requirements: Low/wet basin, floodplain or documented water hazard; not chosen for dry high ground.
items.Generative effects: Raised or avoided grounds, damaged walls, ferries/crossings, wetlands and occasional abandoned construction.
items.Name: Flood-Prone Ground
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor connected floodplains, channels, tidal outlets, actual historic flood risk.

items.Composition interactions: Guild commons, estates and markets contest control; access and reserved land produce downstream street morphology.
items.Core idea: An unusually valuable dependable water source benefits residents and work.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual spring/groundwater-fed water availability and viable access/rights; supernatural healing is not implied.
items.Generative effects: Water commons, public approaches, gardens, baths or productive works when supported; protected source corridor.
items.Name: Reliable Spring
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor real water sources, historical supply disputes, cultivation or crafts requiring dependable water.

items.Composition interactions: Learned services may seek records while tenements reuse shelter and estates preserve monuments; no ungrounded ancient empire.
items.Core idea: Earlier built civilization leaves significant standing or buried remains.
items.Eligibility requirements: Retained existing ruins, recorded ancient works or credible historical material evidence.
items.Generative effects: Broken masonry, reused courts, protected excavation grounds, awkward routes, buried walls.
items.Name: Ancient Ruins
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor known older ruins and reused infrastructure, old tombs or abandoned city strata.

items.Composition interactions: Influences every economic/social combination's access and rights; must consume real historical wall geometry and maintenance.
items.Core idea: A former defensive ring now runs through a newer district.
items.Eligibility requirements: An actual inherited/locally modeled former wall, gate alignment or fortification history.
items.Generative effects: Interior wall fragments, reused old gates, breached/collapsed masonry, market or road alignments around surviving works.
items.Name: Outgrown Wall
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor formerly protected cores and phases of outward settlement growth.

items.Composition interactions: May alter market demand, authority, security or tourism; do not automatically create a palace, title or institution.
items.Core idea: A locally renowned individual or household anchors a district's stories and destinations.
items.Eligibility requirements: Existing named/recorded NPC or supported notable-person event plus a persistent plausible home/role, not an invented public figure.
items.Generative effects: Identifiable seat, home/court/meeting place and possible patronage trails consistent with actual person.
items.Name: Notable Resident
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor actual residence, patrons, guild authority, scholarship, services or notable historical site.

items.Composition interactions: Can burden craft markets or become a boon to patrons; actual fauna remains owned by ecology, not created by district flavor.
items.Core idea: A conspicuous animal or fantastic creature population nests in or beside the quarter.
items.Eligibility requirements: Actual animal species/habitat or magical ecology and nesting/food substrate supported by the world.
items.Generative effects: Distinct nesting areas, sound/nuisance, protected roosts, animal-related POIs/rights where viable.
items.Name: Creature Rookery
items.Provenance: Starter proposal for replacing existing single-list district types; pending Phase 5 reconciliation with old list and production adoption.
items.Weighted suitability: Favor connected roofs, cliffs, groves, refuse/food sources or protected breeding grounds.
